chief_complaint: Chronic musculoskeletal pain (neck and low back) leading to frequent NSAID use
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 33‑year‑old woman with a long‑standing history of chronic neck and low‑back pain since 2014, for which she self‑medicates with ibuprofen. Over the past several years she has developed obesity (documented 2021), stage 2 hypertension (SBP 157/DBP 90), and prediabetes (A1c 6.2%). She reports ongoing stress since early 2021 and has a history of anemia diagnosed in 2016. Social circumstances are challenging: refugee status, unsatisfactory housing, lack of reliable transportation, limited social contact, and a criminal record, all contributing to chronic stress and limited access to care. The last documented encounter was in September 2021, indicating a gap in routine monitoring of her cardiometabolic risk factors.
past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include multiple medication review prompts (2020‑2021), two normal pregnancies (2019, 2021), concussions in 2019 (no loss of consciousness), and gingivitis episodes (2017, 2019). A prior episode of stress resolved in 2020 is also documented.

active_medications.name: Ibuprofen 400 mg oral tablet
active_medications.purpose: Analgesic for chronic neck and low‑back pain

social_determinants: Refugee status; unsatisfactory housing; lack of reliable transportation; limited social contact and social isolation; criminal record; full‑time employment; high‑school education level. These factors contribute to chronic stress, reduced access to care, and barriers to healthy lifestyle adoption.
risk_factor_summary: Cardiovascular risk: stage 2 hypertension (SBP 157/DBP 90), obesity, prediabetes, and anemia place the patient at high 10‑year ASCVD risk. Metabolic risk: prediabetes with A1c 6.2% and obesity. Renal risk: chronic NSAID use without renal function data may predispose to AKI or CKD. Musculoskeletal risk: chronic neck and low‑back pain limiting activity. Hematologic risk: anemia of unclear etiology. Psychosocial risk: high stress, social isolation, housing instability, refugee status, and criminal record increase likelihood of poor medication adherence and unhealthy behaviors. Charlson comorbidity index is 1, clinical complexity moderate.
